item.title: “Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the defilement of beings. Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the purification of beings.” “But,…
item.description:
“Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the defilement of beings. Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the purification of beings.” “But, venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition for the defilement of beings?” “Mahāli, if form were exclusively suffering, immersed in suffering, accompanied by suffering, not accompanied by happiness, beings would not become lustful for form. But because form is happiness, Mahāli, immersed in happiness, accompanied by happiness, not accompanied by suffering, beings become lustful for form. Through lust, they are bound; through being bound, they are defiled. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the defilement of beings. Such being the cause, such being the condition, beings are defiled.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.60

item.title: “Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
item.description:
“Monks, what one intends, what one plans, and what one has a tendency towards — that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a basis, consciousness becomes established. When consciousness is established and grows, there is a leaning (nati). When there is a leaning, there is a going to a state of rebirth. When there is a going to a state of rebirth, there is future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Such is the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no basis, consciousness does not become established. When consciousness is not established and does not grow, there is no leaning. When there is no leaning, there is no going to a state of rebirth. When there is no going to a state of rebirth, there is no future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.40
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Bhalliya: “Who drives away the army of Death, As a great flood sweeps away a frail bridge of reeds — Victorious, fearless, Having subdued,…
item.description:
Elder Bhalliya:
“Who drives away the army of Death,
As a great flood sweeps away a frail bridge of reeds —
Victorious, fearless,
Having subdued, he dwells at peace.”

From: Theragāthā 1.7

item.title: Elder Nun Sumedhā: “What is this foul, stinking body, Frightening, A leather bag full of corpses, Oozing impurities? What is this body I know —…
item.description:
Elder Nun Sumedhā:

“What is this foul, stinking body,
Frightening,
A leather bag full of corpses,
Oozing impurities?

What is this body I know —
Disgusting, smeared with flesh and blood,
A dwelling for worms,
Food for birds —
This body is like that —
To whom should I give it now?

The body, thrown in a charnel ground,
Not long, loses consciousness —
Like a discarded log —
Relatives are disgusted.

That body thrown in the charnel ground,
Becomes food for others —
Formerly they washed it clean,
Now they are disgusted —
Even parents are like that —
What to say of ordinary people?

They are infatuated with a body without core,
Bound by sinews and bones,
Full of saliva and tears,
Full of feces and urine, foul-smelling.

If this body were cut open,
Its inner parts revealed,
Even one’s mother would be disgusted,
Unable to bear the stench.

It is because of aggregates, elements, and sense-bases
That this body is constituted —
The root of renewed existence, suffering —
They speak of it rightly —
They do not delight in it at all.
So who would I wish to marry?

Even a hundred spears every day,
Constantly piercing the body —
Though harmed for a hundred years —
That would still be better,
Because that suffering,
In the end, would be destroyed.

The wise would agree to such killing,
As the Teacher declared —
They wander on for a long time,
With minds given to killing,
Continually following one after another.

In the realms of devas and humans,
Animals, asuras,
Hungry ghosts, and hell —
They undergo endless slaughter.

In hell, there are many —
Those with defiled minds, fallen —
The heavenly realm is no refuge —
There is no Nibbāna-like happiness there.

Those who attain Nibbāna
Are intimately connected
With the teaching
Of the One with Ten Powers —
At ease, unruffled,
Striving to end birth and death.

Today, father, I am determined to leave.
These empty possessions
Are of no value.
I am disgusted with sensual pleasures,
I am weary of sensual pleasures —
They have been cut off,
Like a palm tree stump.”

From: Therīgāthā 16.1
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Then the Blessed One, knowing “This is Māra the Evil One,” recited this verse to Māra: Forms, sounds, tastes, and smells, And all contacts, all…
item.description:
Then the Blessed One, knowing “This is Māra the Evil One,” recited this verse to Māra:
Forms, sounds, tastes, and smells,
And all contacts, all phenomena —
These are terrifying things,
Bewildering beings in the world.
A disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
Mindful, transcends them all,
Transcending Māra’s power,
Shining like the sun.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 4.17
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, I do not see any other hindrance by which beings, hindered, wander and transmigrate for a long time as this hindrance of ignorance. Monks,…
item.description:
“Monks, I do not see any other hindrance by which beings, hindered, wander and transmigrate for a long time as this hindrance of ignorance. Monks, hindered by the hindrance of ignorance, beings wander and transmigrate for a long time.

No other thing so hinders beings,
That they run on by day and night,
As that of delusion’s snare.

But one who has abandoned delusion,
Pierced through the mass of darkness,
No longer wanders on —
In them the cause is no more.”

From: Itivuttaka 14
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “And what, monks, is dwelling heedfully? If one lives without restraint of the eye faculty, monks, his mind is defiled by forms cognizable by the…
item.description:
“And what, monks, is dwelling heedfully? If one lives without restraint of the eye faculty, monks, his mind is defiled by forms cognizable by the eye. For one with a defiled mind, there is no gladness. Without gladness, there is no rapture. Without rapture, there is no tranquility. Without tranquility, suffering remains. For one who is suffering, the mind does not become concentrated. When the mind is not concentrated, phenomena are not clearly seen. When phenomena are not clearly seen, he is called ‘one who dwells heedfully’ … the ear faculty … the nose faculty … the tongue faculty … the body faculty … If one lives without restraint of the mind faculty, his mind is defiled by phenomena cognizable by the mind. For one with a defiled mind, there is no gladness … he is called ‘one who dwells heedfully.’ Thus, monks, is dwelling heedfully.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.97

item.title: Elder Añña-Koṇḍañña: I am exceedingly joyful, Having heard the supreme Dhamma, The Dhamma taught for dispassion, Completely without clinging. In this world of a round…
item.description:
Elder Añña-Koṇḍañña:

I am exceedingly joyful,
Having heard the supreme Dhamma,
The Dhamma taught for dispassion,
Completely without clinging.

In this world of a round earth,
With many colors and forms,
Bewildering the mind —
Thus I thought:
The sign of beauty is very enticing,
Connected with lust.

As wind blows away dust,
As rain settles it down,
Thoughts become stilled
When seen with wisdom.

All conditioned things are impermanent —
When seen with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

All conditioned things are suffering —
When seen with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

All phenomena are not-self —
When seen with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

From: Theragāthā 15.1
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, short indeed is the lifespan of humans in this world — one must go on to the future. Do good, live the holy life.…
item.description:
“Monks, short indeed is the lifespan of humans in this world — one must go on to the future. Do good, live the holy life. For nothing that is born is without death. Monks, a long-lived person lives only a hundred years, or a little more or less.

Human life is short,
The good person should be concerned,
Live as if the head is on fire —
Death will surely come.

Days and nights pass by,
Life span comes to an end,
Human life dries up
Like a stream in the mountains.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 4.9
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Who has conquered the thorn of sensuality, Insult, injury, bondage, That one stands firm, Like a mountain unshaken — Such a monk, Pleasure and pain…
item.description:
Who has conquered the thorn of sensuality,
Insult, injury, bondage,
That one stands firm,
Like a mountain unshaken —
Such a monk,
Pleasure and pain do not disturb.

From: Udana 3.3
